_comment: LIVE pack: real production sites, no credentials, no payments. Run with
python3 bench/run_bench.py --cases bench/cases-live.json --mode-tag live
Deliberately NOT part of bench/smoke.sh: these platforms are external and slow/flaky.
Shapes the fixture pages cannot exercise: 688-2817 interactive elements (Wikipedia),
duplicate labels with no data-test, CJK headings carrying an edit link, one subgoal
needing two actions on one page, duplicate identical nav links (bbc.com /news),
URL-encoded CJK paths, and a shadow-DOM app whose shadow content is invisible to
document.querySelectorAll.
Every signal was verified by hand against the live DOM before being frozen here.
Measured on the live results pages: zero-shot laya cannot clear the pick floor there
(en.wikipedia results page, 1300+ interactive elements: best pick 0.24 < floor 0.25), which is
exactly the documented reason a frozen plan NAMES its target. The article subgoals therefore carry
a target_hint (a[href~Alan_Turing] / the CJK label), and the fill subgoals carry a slots bag --
without it the executor correctly refuses to invent a value (needs_value) rather than guessing.
KNOWN RED -- live-wiki-en-search sg0: en.wikipedia's Codex search widget does not retain a
programmatic fill() (the node is re-rendered; zh.wikipedia's box keeps it), so any signal read
off the field value can never fire. Measured: fill succeeds as rule:match conf 1.00, then
css_value_equals on #searchInput is false and the subgoal stops at low confidence. The fix is a
signal on the EFFECT (the URL/heading after submitting) -- which needs the fill and the submit in
one subgoal, and one subgoal carries one target_hint, so this is a real open design point, not a
typo. Kept in the pack so the next round has the failing evidence.
